title: Positive ordered word map of a morphism to a group scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], let $G$ be a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $\varphi:X\to G$ be a $k$-morphism. For each integer $n\geq0$, the positive ordered word map is the $k$-morphism $w_{n+1}:X^{n+1}\to G$ given by $w_{n+1}(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=\varphi(x_0)\cdots\varphi(x_n)$, where the factors are multiplied in increasing index order and the power is formed over $k$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Equivalently it is the ordered product of the morphisms $\varphi\circ\operatorname{pr}_i$, $0\leq i\leq n$. No assumption that $\varphi$ is a homomorphism or preserves a chosen point is needed to define this map.

source.place: Section 2h, affine-case word map preceding Proposition 2.46, printed pp.54-55; the ordered-word construction itself does not require the affine or pointed hypotheses used for generated-subgroup properties.
